head: 58bcc28
method: Four parallel audits across the core-loop specs, shipped templates and doctrine, the enforcement machinery, and the satellite skills — each classification then attacked by an independent adversarial verifier. RECLASSIFY and REFUTED verdicts are applied here; a classification that did not survive attack was dropped.

rules.title: Red ✅ requires a non-empty `cases` record
rules.statement: A phase whose `cells.red` is `done` must carry a non-empty `phases[].cases` record in .kdbp/PLAN.json, or the PLAN write is rejected.
rules.mechanism: plan-proof-guard.sh PostToolUse hook on Write|Edit|MultiEdit of .kdbp/PLAN.json|PLAN.md; appends a violation and exits 2
rules.exit_semantics: exit 2 + stderr = blocking feedback to the model (the only blocking mechanism in the core loop)
rules.evidence: Read plan-proof-guard.sh:100-134 — `if c.get("red") == "done": cases = (ph.get("cases") or "").strip(); if not cases: out.append(...)` then `if [ -n "${viol:-}" ] … exit 2`. Wired at templates/hooks.json:55-67. Fixtures tests/hooks/run.sh:42-61 prove both FIRE and SILENT.

rules.title: Exec ✅ requires every declared PROOF artifact to exist on disk
rules.statement: When `cells.exec` is `done`, every path named in the phase's `proof` string must resolve on disk (literal path, brace-expanded glob, or non-empty parent dir) or the PLAN write is blocked.
rules.mechanism: plan-proof-guard.sh splits `proof` on ' · ' and '→', strips a trailing '(n shots)', and calls evidence_exists() on the last segment; exit 2 on any miss
rules.exit_semantics: exit 2 = blocking feedback; proof:null passes; a token with no concrete path component is never evidence
rules.evidence: Read plan-proof-guard.sh:112-121. Header at :6-11 states the R2 shorthand tolerance. Fixture battery tests/hooks/run.sh:43-66 covers empty-evidence-dir BLOCK, bare `*` BLOCK, and the round-4 cap-tripped multi-brace PASS.

rules.title: A cited `red@<sha>` must be a reachable commit
rules.statement: Every `red@<7-40 hex>` token inside a Red-✅ phase's `cases` record must resolve via `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` or the PLAN write is blocked.
rules.mechanism: plan-proof-guard.sh sha_reachable() shells out to `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}`, caches the result, and appends a violation on failure
rules.exit_semantics: exit 2 = blocking feedback
rules.evidence: Read plan-proof-guard.sh:93-111: `for sha in re.findall(r"red@([0-9a-f]{7,40})", cases): if not sha_reachable(sha): out.append(...)`. red-spec.md:82-84 states the guard's exact scope: 'the plan-proof-guard validates that a cases record EXISTS and that every sha it CITES is reachable — a record citing no sha passes; the hook never re-runs tests'.

rules.title: PLAN.md Phases-table cell glyph vocabulary is closed
rules.statement: Every Phases-table cell must be one of ⬜ 🔄 ✅ ⏸ ⚰️ (or `—` for a render-only Red cell); an unknown glyph aborts mirror regeneration without touching the existing mirror.
rules.mechanism: regen-mirror.py GLYPH dict lookup; `sys.exit(f"BREAK: phase {pid} {cname} cell {glyph!r} is not a known glyph")`; the JSON write is the last statement so a BREAK leaves the old mirror intact
rules.exit_semantics: exit 1 (SystemExit carrying a BREAK: message); also exit 1 at :26 (no PLAN.md) and :67 (no Phases table header)
rules.evidence: grep -n 'GLYPH|BREAK|sys.exit' regen-mirror.py returns :21 (the map), :26, :67, :156-157. Fixtures tests/plan-mirror/run.sh (41 assertions) cover both BREAK exits and untouched-mirror-on-BREAK. Caveat: nothing auto-invokes the script — /gabe-plan runs it per plan-spec.md:499.

rules.title: PLAN.json cell tokens are a closed 5-value enum (router refusal)
rules.statement: Every `phases[].cells` value must be one of todo|in_progress|done|deferred|obsolete; any other token makes the router refuse the mirror rather than route on it.
rules.mechanism: next.mjs iterates every cell and calls process.exit(2) on a token outside GLYPH; also exits 2 on non-array phases, a null phase entry, and current_phase desync
rules.exit_semantics: exit 2 = PLAN.json unusable → caller falls back to prose PLAN.md routing (degrade, not block); exit 1 = no active plan; exit 0 = decision printed
rules.evidence: Read next.mjs:15,35-59 — the comment at :44-45 gives the rationale: 'A mistyped cell token ("Done", "complete") is neither todo nor done — it would silently route wrong … Refuse the mirror instead.' Fixtures tests/hooks/run.sh:145-158 (8 assertions incl. all four exit-2 refusals).

rules.title: scope-session.json / scope-references.yaml are JSON-Schema validated
rules.statement: Both /gabe-scope state artifacts must validate against Draft 2020-12 schemas; a schema violation aborts the run and a validator that cannot run is an E6 STOP, never a pass.
rules.mechanism: schemas/validate.py using jsonschema Draft202012Validator, plus a dependency preflight that turns a missing pyyaml/jsonschema into a one-line 'GATE CANNOT RUN' rather than a traceback
rules.exit_semantics: exit 0 = VALID · exit 1 = INVALID (per-path errors printed) · exit 2 = harness/dependency failure = E6 STOP
rules.evidence: scope-spec.md:464 'Validate the session.json against schemas/scope-session.schema.json after every write. Schema violation = abort'; :466 'Validator exit 2 … = E6 STOP: a gate that could not run has proven nothing, so the run stops — it does NOT pass.' scope-spec.md:99 'reject on schema failure' for references. All three exits fixture-proven by tests/scope-schema/run.sh (18 assertions).

rules.title: Skip-code enum claimed byte-identical — five divergent renderings
rules.statement: The suite declares the auto-tick skip code a byte-identical cross-skill contract, but the enum has four mutually different renderings and no diff check exists.
rules.mechanism: none
rules.evidence: grep -rln 'byte-identical' over scripts/ and tests/ returns nothing — no checker exists. The four renderings: plan-spec.md:793 six codes (no-plan | not-active | phase-not-found | column-missing | legacy-format | footer-mismatch); gate-spec.md:304 five codes (drops not-active); mechanisms.md:326-327 four codes with a different prefix (`ℹ <file>: <column>` not `ℹ PLAN: <col>`) plus an invented code `pointer-mismatch`; review-spec.md:981 a fifth free-form string `ℹ PLAN: phase tick skipped (diff MISALIGNED with current phase scope)`. Repo-wide grep confirms `pointer-mismatch` and `not-active` each occur exactly once.  [verified: docs/src/mechanisms.md:38 says these strings are "written once, copied byte-identical wherever they appear, never paraphrased"; :46 lists the skip code as one; :53 says "Byte-identical reuse turns a cross-file agreement into something a plain-text diff can verify." No diff exists: `grep -rln 'byte-identical' scripts/ tests/` returns only tests/plan-mirror/run.sh and tests/red-sweep/run.sh, and bot]
rules.hardening: Extract the enum to one shared anchor and assert set-equality across its carriers — the suite center already computes the per-file member sets and the missing-vs-union diff (_suite_formats.enum_variants).
rules.defect: The only one of the eight shared strings that fails the diff. Five distinct renderings: gate-spec.md:304 (5 members, drops not-active, reorders two); plan-spec.md:793 (6 members, the canonical list); execute-spec.md:294 emits `(tasks-block-missing)`, a code in no enum anywhere; review-spec.md:981 emits `(diff MISALIGNED with current phase scope)`, free text where the contract specifies an enum member; mechanisms.md:46 states the template itself. Two of the five are therefore not enum members at all.

rules.title: 33-tag closed Types list contradicted one line later by its own spec

rules.mechanism: none — only next.mjs's 6-value MOCKUP_TAGS subset is machine-consumed; nothing validates membership in the 33-tag list
rules.evidence: plan-spec.md:132 enumerates the 33 tags. plan-spec.md:133 then keys runtime journey evidence on {user-facing, native-mobile, mobile-web, web, upload, realtime, streaming, file-media, auth, session, notifications}; execute-spec.md:64 uses that set plus DB; review-spec.md:179 the same minus DB. Six of those (native-mobile, mobile-web, web, file-media, notifications, DB) are absent from the closed list at :132. next.mjs:12-14 hardcodes only MOCKUP_TAGS; regen-mirror.py:95-97,126,142 parses `types` and writes it through with no membership test.  [verified: plan-spec.md:132 confirmed verbatim, including 'Tags MUST come from the canonical closed list' and 'Freeform tags (`frontend`, `ui-screens`) silently disable /gabe-next hybrid dispatch and /gabe-execute evidence classification — reject them and re-ask.' The 33-tag set contains no native-mobile, mobile-web, web, file-media, notifications or DB. plan-spec.md:133, execute-spec.md:64 and review-spec.m]
rules.defect: plan-spec.md:132 states 'Tags MUST come from the canonical closed list … Freeform tags (`frontend`, `ui-screens`) silently disable `/gabe-next` hybrid dispatch and `/gabe-execute` evidence classification — reject them and re-ask.' A planner obeying that sentence literally produces a plan whose Types can never trip the runtime-evidence classifier at plan-spec.md:133 / execute-spec.md:64 / review-spec.md:179, because six of the trigger tags are not legal tags. The stated consequence is also inverted: using the six 'illegal' tags is precisely what ENABLES evidence classification.

rules.mechanism: none
rules.evidence: Citations: plan-spec.md:179, :186, :330; review-spec.md:503; push-spec.md:306; plus U8 at templates/tier-sections/ai-agent.md:19. The only U-numbered list in the repo is skills/gabe-assess/references/align-spec.md:65-67, an EXAMPLE of a user-authored ~/.claude/VALUES.md running U1–U3 (Verify Before Shipping / Say Why / Two Roads) — it contains no U4 and no U8. U4's full title ('Enforce Output Structure Mechanically') appears exactly once, in a tier-section table cell at templates/tier-sections/ai-agent.md:20, not in any catalog.  [REFUTED as BROKEN_CLAIM, corrected to PROMPT_ONLY: Residual, much smaller finding: the align-spec:65-67 example is STALE (it shows U1–U3 as 'Verify Before Shipping / Say Why / Two Roads'; the real file reads 'Prove It Works / Plan Light, Build Real / One Thread'), the real catalog has NO U7 while init-spec.md:304 instructs 'Add U4-U8 to project VALUES.md', and nothing mechanically asserts the user-level catalog is present before a spec cites it. That is a PROMPT_ONLY anchor-resolution gap, not a broken claim.]
rules.defect: skills/gabe-docs/references/execution-contract.md:18 defines E6 as 'MISSING ANCHOR = STOP' — a referenced template/spec/catalog that is absent must print ⛔ and stop. plan-spec.md:330 reads '(per U4 — downstream consumers read structure, not prose)' and review-spec.md:503 reads '(PydanticAI `output_type` or equivalent — user value U4)'. Both resolve to nothing. By the suite's own contract every run that tries to resolve U4 should halt; instead the citation reads as an authority the reader assumes exists.

rules.title: plan-spec calls a prose rendering rule a 'U4-level enforcement point'
rules.statement: The tier-table rendering invariants are declared a mechanical enforcement point that must not rely on prompt instructions, while being enforced by nothing but prompt instructions.
rules.mechanism: none
rules.evidence: plan-spec.md:179 heads the block '**Rendering invariants (runtime behaviour, U4 mechanical enforcement):**'. skills/gabe-plan/ ships exactly one script, scripts/regen-mirror.py, which parses the Phases table and the Phase Details YAML and contains no check on section-table header order, row-body order, or prose placement. No hook, checker or battery touches Step 3.5.2 output.  [verified: plan-spec.md:179 confirmed verbatim: '**Rendering invariants (runtime behaviour, U4 mechanical enforcement):**'; :186 confirmed verbatim: 'This is a U4-level enforcement point: do not rely on prompt instructions to hold the line at runtime. When emitting Step 3.5.2 output, the renderer emits the section table header first, then the full row body, then prose commentary after. Any deviation is a bug]

When emitting Step 3.5.2 output, the renderer emits the section table header first, then the full row body, then prose commentary after. Any deviation is a bug.' rules.title: review 5b sub-call declared PydanticAI `output_type`-structured

rules.title: PROOF line format is unverified; the guard skips odd wordings

rules.exit_semantics: exit 2 only when a QUALIFYING segment names a missing path; a non-qualifying proof string exits 0
rules.evidence: Read plan-proof-guard.sh:114-116: `if isinstance(proof, str) and "→" in proof:` … `if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[0].upper().startswith("PROOF")`. A proof of `":<port> desktop+mobile proof"` — the exact FAIL example given at review-spec.md:198 — contains no arrow, so the guard never inspects it and the Exec ✅ lands. The string is listed as a byte-identical producer≡consumer contract at docs/src/mechanisms.md:41 with no diff check.  [verified: plan-proof-guard.sh:112-121 read verbatim: the whole inspection is gated on `if isinstance(proof, str) and "→" in proof:` then, per ' · ' segment, `if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[0].upper().startswith("PROOF")`. Anything failing either test falls through silently and the Exec ✅ stands. review-spec.md:198 confirmed as the FAIL exemplar: 'FAIL: `proof: ":<port> desktop+mobile proof"` — a claim with no]
rules.hardening: In plan-proof-guard.sh, when `cells.exec == "done"` and `proof` is a non-null string, first require every ' · '-joined segment to match `^PROOF: .+ → .+ → .+` and append a violation when it does not — turning today's silent skip into the same exit-2 path. Fixture: a phase with `proof: ":8080 desktop proof"` and exec done must BLOCK.

rules.title: M[N] is reserved for myopic findings; C[N] is reserved corpus-wide for case ids
rules.statement: When gabe-myopic numbers findings — in the report, in PLAN/PENDING prose, or carried into regression-test titles — it uses the M[N] family and never C[N], because C[N] is the global case-id family owned by gabe-red.
rules.mechanism: partial and opt-in: backfill-sweep.py renames an ENUMERATED colliding-label set via --myopic-labels=, and the C-id regexes are anchored so an M-token can never be read as a case id

Never `C[N]`: that prefix is reserved corpus-wide for case ids (gabe-red red-spec), and scenario labels are per-report, so a `C`-labeled scenario collides with the global case family on the next walk." Machine support is remediation-only and operator-driven: backfill-sweep.py:5 documents `--myopic-labels=C1,C4`, :10-12 states the set is ENUMERATED and never an open pattern, :67 does the rename. So a violation is FIXABLE by hand once someone notices; it is not DETECTABLE — nothing tells a `C1` authored by myopic from a `C1` authored by red. Also documented on the public site at docs/src/c-id.md:56. Carrier is excellent: the lean core, in the mode section, where the labels are minted.

rules.title: Satellite frontmatter flags carry the fork/read-only/human-only contracts and no check verifies their spelling
rules.statement: Satellite skills declare their execution contract in frontmatter — context: fork (satellite analyses), agent: Explore (read-only runs), disable-model-invocation: true (human-initiated only), user-invocable: false (background knowledge), paths: (auto-trigger globs).

rules.exit_semantics: suite-doctor report() → drift=1 → exit 1; no flag reaches that path

A typo — `context: forked`, `disable_model_invocation` — silently converts a human-only or read-only skill into a normally-dispatchable one, and every gate in the repo still reports CLEAN. rules.title: Human-initiated-only skills are gated by the harness, not by anything in the repo
rules.statement: /gabe-cc-init, /gabe-init and /gabe-scope-pivot may not be invoked by the model — they require a human to type them.
rules.mechanism: Claude Code frontmatter `disable-model-invocation: true` — the harness suppresses model dispatch of the skill
rules.exit_semantics: harness-level dispatch suppression; no exit code, nothing repo-side observes it
rules.evidence: All three files carry `disable-model-invocation: true` on line 5 (verified by grep across skills/gabe-*/SKILL.md). This is the one rule in this family enforced by a machine rather than by prose — but the machine is the harness, outside this repo, so the repo cannot prove it fired, and nothing in the repo asserts the key is spelled correctly or still present (see the frontmatter-vocabulary finding above: suite-doctor.sh:113 reads only `version`). The safety weight is real: gabe-cc-init's init mode `git mv`s a project's entire doc tree into docs/_archive/ (skills/gabe-cc-init/references/adopt-spec.md:61-65), and gabe-scope-pivot rewrites a project's scope. The declaration is the whole guard.

rules.title: Fork satellites promise read-only behavior that no mechanism can bind
rules.statement: gabe-health is read-only: it never modifies files, never blocks commits or PRs, and does not require .kdbp/ to exist; the same fork/read-only posture is declared by roast, debt and myopic.
rules.mechanism: none
rules.evidence: SKILL.md:19: "Read-only: never modifies files, never blocks commits or PRs, does not require `.kdbp/` to exist." Same posture at skills/gabe-roast/SKILL.md:5-6 and skills/gabe-health/SKILL.md:5-6 (context: fork + agent: Explore), and skills/gabe-myopic/SKILL.md:5. No hook can bind it: the two Write-side hooks (scripts/hooks/kdbp/post-structure-warning.sh, plan-proof-guard.sh, wired at templates/hooks.json:42-67) receive a tool_input and have no signal for which skill is executing, so 'a fork satellite must not Write' is not expressible as a check. This is genuinely PROMPT_ONLY, not payable debt. Note the honest counter-example inside the same family: gabe-health is declared fork/Explore at :5-6 yet its default mode WRITES to four .kdbp targets (SKILL.md:46) — the read-only posture applies to its brief/dry-run/audit-rules/extract-rules modes only (:29-31), a distinction carried entirely by the mode table.

rules.title: gabe-cc-init: archive, never delete
rules.statement: Adoption never deletes anything — archived material moves by `git mv` into docs/_archive/<date>-pre-adoption/ with an explanatory README, and machine sources (tests, junit/results, .kdbp/, root README, source code) are never even offered for archive.
rules.mechanism: none
rules.evidence: SKILL.md:50: "Does NOT delete anything, ever — archive is `git mv` plus an explanatory README." The deep procedure is references/adopt-spec.md:57-65: the operator marks each inventory row KEEP or ARCHIVE (:57), "Machine sources are never offered for archive: tests, junit/results, `.kdbp/`, root README, source code" (:58), and on approval `git mv` each row plus an archive README — "**archived, never deleted**" (:61-65). Nothing observes the file operations; the only structural protection is that the skill is human-initiated (disable-model-invocation, :5) and that the archive list is a checkpoint requiring operator approval before any move (SKILL.md:24 Gate column). Carrier is layered correctly: the law in the lean core's Non-goals, the procedure in the deep spec.

rules.title: gabe-cc-init: one section per run, and a request to batch is refused
rules.statement: Adoption ingests exactly ONE entity section per invocation and refuses a request to batch sections — human-speed review IS the feature; each section closes on operator approval recorded as a walk (`adopt:<slug>`).
rules.mechanism: none
rules.evidence: SKILL.md:39: "**One section per run, by design.** A request to batch sections is refused — human-speed review IS the feature." The gate for `section <entity>` is "Operator approval, recorded as a walk (`adopt:<entity>`)" (:26), and gabe-walk confirms the convention from its side: "`/gabe-cc-init` approvals record `adopt:<slug>`; the center credits both to the entity's manual angle" (skills/gabe-walk/SKILL.md:23). The tracker's per-section checklist (adopt-spec.md:35: testing_inventory, legacy_reverified, card, diagrams, proofs, gate_green, walk_recorded) is a data record with no validator — adoption.json has no schema and no battery anywhere (audit_raw.md:212). A batched run would leave an adoption.json that looks exactly like several honest ones.

rules.title: gabe-cc-init's tracker never lives in PLAN.md and /gabe-next never reads it
rules.statement: The adoption tracker lives at docs/site/center/adoption.json, never in PLAN.md; /gabe-next and the active plan are untouched by the adoption track.
rules.mechanism: none as a rule; structurally true today because next.mjs reads only .kdbp/PLAN.json
rules.evidence: SKILL.md:40: "**The tracker never lives in PLAN.md.** `/gabe-next` and the active plan are untouched; adoption is the parallel back-catalog track." Restated at adopt-spec.md:49. The router genuinely cannot see it — next.mjs parses PLAN.json's phases/cells only (per the prior audit at audit_raw.md:254-258, whose exit-2 refusals are fixture-covered in tests/hooks/run.sh:145-158) — so today the separation holds by construction rather than by check. What is unguarded is the inverse: nothing stops an adoption row being smuggled INTO PLAN.md's Phases table, where regen-mirror.py would copy it into the mirror without complaint (it validates glyphs, not row semantics).

rules.title: gabe-walk: brief the walker BEFORE recording, from committed data only
rules.statement: A walk has two halves — the walker is first briefed (why this walk · what this thing is from the card's HANDLE/WHAT & WHY · the FLOWS itinerary joined against archmap coverage · what pass/partial/fail mean here), and only then are the four questions asked; every briefing item with no source is named absent, never padded.
rules.mechanism: none
rules.evidence: SKILL.md:24-29 carries the whole contract: "**Brief the walker** — a walk request must never be a mystery. Before any question, assemble and show (all from committed data — E1; each item that has no source is named absent, never padded)", the four bullets, and the closing line "A walker who stops after the briefing leaves NO record." The unproven-flow line at :27 ("your eyes are the only verification this flow has") is the point of the whole beat. The record written at :31-34 has NO field for the briefing — a walk recorded without a brief is byte-identical on walks.jsonl to one that was fully briefed. So the discipline is unfalsifiable after the fact by construction, not by oversight. Carrier is ideal: gabe-walk has no references/ at all (44 lines total), so the entire binding contract is in the always-loaded lean core.

rules.title: walks.jsonl's record shape is declared inline and validated nowhere

rules.title: gabe-walk records, never judges — and never records on an agent's behalf
rules.statement: The walker is the human: the skill never invents a subject, never records 'walked' on an agent's behalf, never verifies the evidence path's contents, and never computes staleness — a subject with zero records renders NEVER-walked red until someone actually walks it.
rules.mechanism: none
rules.evidence: SKILL.md:23: "This skill never invents a subject and never records 'walked' on an agent's behalf — the walker is the human (E6: no subject, no record)." Reinforced at :17 ("A synthesized witness is worse than an honest gap") and by the Non-goals at :40-41 (does not verify the evidence path's contents; does not compute staleness). The identity default is `git config user.name` (:30), which is exactly the value a model would also produce — so the record cannot distinguish a human walk from a fabricated one. This is the load-bearing honesty rule of the verification-first design and it is, irreducibly, an honour system: no mechanism can witness a witness.

rules.title: gabe-cc-entity's unknown-slug STOP is a real refusal the model is told to surface verbatim
rules.statement: The three center sources (archmap.json + adoption.json + center.config.json) join on the entity slug; an unknown slug, a missing center, or absent data STOPs with the available-entity list and never yields a fabricated pack.

The refusal itself is mechanical and reproducible.

Compliance is therefore real and recent — and entirely voluntary: no script inspects a commit message, and skills/gabe-commit/scripts/ holds only size-budget.sh, docs-budget.sh and evidence-freshness.sh, none of which reads the message. If anything mechanical is wanted here it is not a gate but a prompt-side obligation in /gabe-commit's checklist; the only genuinely checkable fragment ('the message contains a Verification block with digits') does not distinguish a real dry-run from an invented one.]
